identity.title: The Formation Height of Millimeter-wavelength Emission in the Solar Chromosphere

paper_type_evidence.quote: We study the formation of ALMA diagnostics using a 2.5D radiative MHD model that includes the effects of ion-neutral interactions (ambipolar diffusion) and non-equilibrium ionization of hydrogen and helium.

targets.name: Plage/network region in 2.5D Bifrost simulations (gol_lte, gol_nei); observed chromospheric hole region (ALMA band 3, 2017/04/27)

evidence.quote: The IRIS observing program was centered at heliocentric coordinates of 170$''$, -210$''$

question.value: Where in the solar atmosphere do ALMA band 3 and band 6 emission form in rMHD models with ambipolar diffusion and non-equilibrium ionization, and how well does brightness temperature trace gas temperature?

evidence.quote: Key for the interpretation of solar ALMA observations is understanding where in the solar atmosphere the ALMA emission originates.
We used the publicly available data ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00202.S.
he ALMA interferometric data were acquired on 2017/04/27 in Band 3 (at 3mm, i.e., 100 GHz) in configuration C40-3
in configuration C40-3

time_on_source.value: 10.5 minute scans, 2 s integration, 37 min total within 16:00-16:45 UT

evidence.quote: ALMA obtained 10.5 minute scans separated by 2min calibration scans, with 2s integration time, for a total of 37min within 16:00-16:45 UT (45 minutes).
he ALMA interferometric data were acquired on 2017/04/27 in Band 3

provided.value: Mg II k 2796 Å spectroheliogram and SJI of same region

evidence.quote: Both ALMA and IRIS observed the same region through a coordinated ALMA/IRIS campaign
The SDO/HMI magnetograms (panel B and green contours) confirm that these fibrils do indeed connect to a strong magnetic field region

what.value: ALMA band 3 observations and analysis of chromospheric holes

evidence.quote: Further details of the ALMA observational analysis can be found in (cite: Loukitcheva:2019ApJ...877L..26L).

what.value: Mean Tb difference between ALMA bands of 1400 K over whole Sun

evidence.quote: This is similar to the difference in mean brightness temperature between the two ALMA bands of 1400 K in the veraged over the whole Sun (cite: White:2017SoPh..292...88W).

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Bifrost 2.5D rMHD simulations gol_lte and gol_nei, 90 Mm wide, 14 km horizontal grid, -3 to 40 Mm height, ~190 G mean field plage

evidence.quote: The horizontal resolution is uniform with a $14$ km grid spacing
Further details on the setup and analysis of these two simulations can be found in (cite: Martinez-Sykora:2019hhegol)
Further details of the ALMA observational analysis can be found in (cite: Loukitcheva:2019ApJ...877L..26L).

method.value: LTE module of STiC computes continuum opacity and emergent intensity at 1.2 and 3 mm from simulation electron density and gas pressure

evidence.quote: STiC utilizes the electron densities and gas pressure stratifications from the simulations to compute the partial densities of all species that are involved in the calculations.

assumptions.value: Free-free hydrogen absorption main opacity source

evidence.quote: which include the main opacity source at mm wavelengths (free-free hydrogen absorption

analysis_steps.goal: Compute tau=1 formation heights and compare Tb with gas temperature

method.value: Optical depth at 1.2 and 3 mm, tau=1 heights averaged over 12 minutes, JPDFs of Tb vs T, contribution and source functions, comparison with VAL-C

evidence.quote: we computed the optical depth ($\tau$) at 1.2 and 3mm wavelengths (ALMA bands 6 and 3, respectively).
For comparison we add, for both ALMA wavelengths, the height at which the optical depth is unity for a VAL-C (cite: Vernazza:1981yq) atmosphere

used_for.value: Synthetic ALMA intensities in LTE module

evidence.quote: we used the LTE module in the tockholm inversion code (STiC) code
These simulations have been calculated with the 3D rMHD *Bifrost* code
To analyze the data we have used IDL.
the average formation height at wavelengths of 1.2mm is 0.9 Mm (with a standard deviation of 0.7 Mm)
the average formation height at 3mm is 1.8 Mm (standard deviation of 1 Mm)
n average the 1.2mm emission is formed at a height of $2.67\pm1.08$ Mm
the 3mm emission is formed at a mean height of $2.78\pm1.09$ Mm

results_numeric.quantity: Mean Tb difference 3 mm vs 1.2 mm, NEI

evidence.loc: Relationship between ALMA brightness temperature and plasma temperature
evidence.quote: The mean brightness temperature difference between the two wavelengths is $1280$ K.

findings_qualitative.value: In NEI both bands form at similar heights in the upper chromosphere, mostly in spicules and fibrils along canopy fields

evidence.quote: In our NEI model, the formation height of ALMA at both wavelengths occurs at greater heights than in LTE models.

claims.hypothesis: Do bands 3 and 6 form at significantly different heights?
claims.experiment: tau=1 heights from LTE and NEI rMHD simulations
claims.finding: With NEI both bands form at similar upper-chromospheric heights

evidence.quote: The difference in average formation heights of these wavelengths is thus $0.11\pm0.3$ Mm.

claims.hypothesis: Can chromospheric holes be explained by cool low-lying loops?
claims.experiment: Compare simulations with ALMA, IRIS, SDO observations
claims.result: Fibril-like features in all three; simulated loops reach 3500-4500 K
claims.finding: Holes may be cool sub-threads in low-lying loops

evidence.quote: This is very similar to what is reported for “chromospheric holes” by (cite: Loukitcheva:2019ApJ...877L..26L).

limitations_admitted.value: Model is 2D and may limit LOS superposition

evidence.quote: We note that our model is limited to two dimensions, and it is crucial to expand this model into 3D.
